sharedEditsNeeded: The avformat backends map every filter parse error to exit status 1. Native exits 256-EINVAL (234 on Linux) for invalid colours and booleans and 256-ERANGE (222) for out-of-range floats. Reporting them needs a shared way for a VideoFilterParseError (or a subclass) to carry an exit status that the media and timed backends turn into ExecutionError.exitCode; @edge-ffmpeg/avfilter cannot import ExecutionError from @edge-ffmpeg/core. Until then the tests assert native's status and EdgeFFmpeg's refusal before output with status 1.
notes: Status partial: the [THREADS] rule cannot hold for native chromakey at the default thread count. do_chromakey_slice resets its u/v windows to the key at each slice start, so native output for frames taller than one row depends on the host CPU count (measured: default vs -filter_threads 1 differ at 4 vCPUs on 17x9, 7x5 and 5x3 yuva420p). The module implements the one-slice result and accepts it only where native is thread-independent: one-row frames, or the generic filter option threads=1, which pins native to one slice (measured equal at default, 1 and 3 filter threads). Taller chromakey without threads=1 is refused in geometry() on every path and again in frame(). chromahold is thread-independent and complete.
chromahold blend ramps (128 + (u - 128) * f, a multiply-add) are gated to linux-x64 as a precaution; no macOS difference has been measured. chromakey has no multiply-add and runs on every platform.
Everything ran only on the sandbox Linux x86_64 build; no macOS run.
Setup: Node 24.22.3 installed from nodejs.org in the scratchpad (sandbox Node was 22.23.5 and bootstrap requires 24); bootstrap 195 s; baseline typecheck+lint+boundaries+registry test 61 s, green.
